text:
maya: FYI nightly evals 03/16-03/18 showing intermittent timeouts, ~4-6 failures per run, looks nondeterministic.

devon: yep noticed that too. failures always in quantized sampling tests, workers get killed after the harness timeout. logs show missed heartbeats from the scheduler.

jonah: can you paste a snippet of the worker logs? is it the usual mmap fd leak or something new?

maya: here's a typical sequence:
```
[2026-03-17T04:12:01Z] worker-23: starting eval batch id=4472
[2026-03-17T04:12:06Z] worker-23: sample loop enter
[2026-03-17T04:12:08Z] scheduler: no heartbeat from worker-23 for 12500ms, marking DEAD
[2026-03-17T04:12:09Z] harness: killed worker-23 (timeout)
```
Looks like the scheduler threshold is 12.5s but worker heartbeats arrive every 10s normally.

lee: interesting — infra-bot also emitted heartbeat alerts around the same time: `infra-bot: worker-heartbeat-monitor detected gap > 10s across pods in us-west2`

infra-bot: ALERT: heartbeat_gap_detected service=heartbeat-monitor region=us-west2 gap_ms=12532 affected=3

devon: hypothesis: container CPU throttling or host load causing the process to not wake to send heartbeat, so scheduler marks it dead. would explain nondeterminism and why only quantized runs (longer per-token ops) hit it.

jonah: could also be mismatch between scheduler using wall-clock vs worker using monotonic time. if one uses system clock and NTP adjusts that could create negative deltas or sudden jumps. any clock drift in host metrics?

maya: I checked host metrics: small NTP step at 04:11:55 (~20ms), nothing that explains 12s. but kube node had a 30s CPUPressure spike around 04:12:05.

devon: patch idea: make heartbeat based on monotonic clock on both sides + add jitter and a small grace window (current grace 2s). also increase default threshold to 20s for long-running sampling tests.

jonah: agree. quick mitigation: bump scheduler.deadline_ms to 20000 in prod config and roll canary to reduce noise, then follow with proper monotonic-based fix.

devon: created a tiny PR with config bump: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/PR/3245 — includes tests for monotonic check.

ci-bot: PR 3245: config/heartbeat: bump deadline_ms -> 20000 by devon. CI: unit (✅), integration (flaky) — rerun recommended.

maya: good. i repro'ed locally by adding sleep(0.015) in the sampling loop which pushes heartbeat past 12s in our harness. reproducer script attached: 
```
# repro: simulate heavy per-token work
python simulate_slow_worker.py --token-delay-ms 15 --heartbeat-interval-ms 10000
```

lee: can we also add a test in the harness that simulates scheduler load and ensures worker isn't falsely marked dead? would help catch regressions in future.

devon: adding integration test that fuzzes heartbeat latency and asserts no false positives under realistic sampling delays.

jonah: assign follow-ups: devon -> PR and integration test, eng-infra -> investigate node CPU throttling patterns, maya -> merge canary bump and monitor nightly runs.

maya: merging canary now, will watch the next 3 nightlies. thanks all :thumbsup:

lee: leaving a note in the eval runbook about heartbeat thresholds + link to this thread.

maya: summary: root cause likely timing/host-load induced delayed heartbeats; short-term config increase deployed; longer-term fix tracked in PR to use monotonic timing and resilient grace window.

jonah: please add the reproducer to the ticket for postmortem.

infra-bot: ACTION_LOG: created issue infra/heartbeat-investigation-789 assigned to eng-infra,priority=medium

maya: closing thread once we confirm nightlies stabilize.
